summary.headline: H1 FY27 standalone revenue at INR 151 crores vs INR 161 crores a year earlier; order book INR 612 crores, up ~39-40% YoY.
summary.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as a soft first half, with standalone revenue slipping from INR 161 crores to INR 151 crores while consolidated H1 growth was claimed on profit and EBITDA. Capacity utilisation was 78.6% across standalone (21,110 MT) and NS Engineering (22,424 MT). The order book stands at INR 612 crores, with a 22% railway / 78% infrastructure split, and a new wagon order conversion with a 30% option clause was won in October. The Amzen (ex-Amtek subsidiary) acquisition remains pending NCLT procedural approval after the Supreme Court win, with the company having paid INR 32 crores upfront and INR 28 crores as security deposit. Management reiterated 20-25% FY27 revenue growth target.

segments.name: Standalone (Cosmic CRF, Singur)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 55,000 MT per annum; H1 FY27 revenue INR 151 crores vs INR 161 crores a year earlier. Produced 21,110 MT in H1.

segments.name: NS Engineering Projects (infra, galvanising)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 65,000 MT; produced 22,424 MT in H1. Galvanising capacity raised from 8,500 MT to 12,000 MT, with air-wiping facility under way.

segments.name: Cosmic Springs and Engineers
segments.commentary: Installed capacity 13,600 MT, expected to reach 24,000-25,000 MT by end FY27 as forging is added. RDSO approval received; field trials pending (approx. 3,000 sets over six months).

segments.name: Forging unit (under set-up)
segments.commentary: Planned capacity 10,000-11,000 MT with INR 45-50 crores investment; commercial runs targeted April-May 2027. Management estimates INR 115-120 crores turnover at 14-15% PAT margin.

segments.name: Amzen (pending NCLT approval)
segments.commentary: Wagon plant with RDSO-assessed capacity of 3,600 wagons (scalable to 7,200); about 150,000 MT capacity cited. Upfront INR 32 crores plus INR 28 crores security deposit paid; first production targeted about three months after approval.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of 20-25% over FY26, reiterated by management despite H1 softness.
Management expects H2 to be stronger, with Q3 and Q4 seasonally better, and plans to push out carried stock in Q3.
Amzen: 25% of capacity (about 37,000-38,000 MT, about INR 400 crores) targeted in FY28; 75% of current installed capacity in FY29; 70% of 150,000 MT by FY30.
Management's illustrative base-case plan of INR 1,178 crores revenue (range INR 1,150-1,300 crores) at 80% utilisation of 175,000 MT without Amzen, with PAT of 12-14%; not formal guidance.
Main board migration: paid-up capital and share requirement (1 crore shares) expected to be met after warrant and swap listings; BSE process expected to conclude around Q4 FY27.
No equity dilution for capital raising until FY28, per management.
capex_capacity: Forging unit: INR 45-50 crores investment to reach about 11,000 MT; set-up delayed 2-2.5 months by rain; commercial runs targeted April-May 2027.
Springs capacity 13,600 MT rising to 24,000-25,000 MT by end FY27 once forging is added (per management).
Galvanising capacity 12,000 MT (from 8,500 MT); air-wiping facility expected to be announced by end of November 2026.

Amzen refurbishment: 392 machines; plan includes AMC contracts, transformer and CNC refurbishment, civil work; about 12 people team based in Jalandhar/Ludhiana. Analysis due by December end; production three to four months after completion.
Total installed capacity 133,600 MT today, targeted at 174,600-175,000 MT including Amzen's ~150,000 MT (management said FY27-FY30 window, not FY30 only).
demand_pricing: Order book INR 612 crores: 22% railway, 78% infrastructure; management says a balanced 50:50 mix is normal.
Railway orders slowed due to fiscal constraints and West Asia crisis; BOXNHL orders back on track (about 9,000 BOXNHL wagons cited).
New wagon order (conversion of old order plus 30% option clause) of roughly INR 900-1,000 crores (stated as INR 9,000-10,000 crore in transcript) and 10,000 wagons, received end of October 2026.
Management says two orders already won from listed wagon makers; will be posted after Diwali pending clearance.
Spring economics: management estimates sale price about INR 30,000 per set vs cost INR 22,500, implying around 15% PAT margin; Raftar conversion demand expected to lift volumes.
Container manufacturing scheme (INR 10,000 crores subsidy) cited as supportive; management expects container demand to rise from 1 lakh to about 5 lakh units.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone other expenses rise despite lower court overheads?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Supreme Court hearing costs (lawyers and depositions) after losing NCLAT in March 2026 were high; H2 FY27 legal costs expected to be much lower.

qa_highlights.question: Why forging, and will the company move into wheelsets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not plan wheelsets; forging aims to backward-integrate 38+ wagon and coach items, support defence R&D, and earn 15-20% margins on RDSO-based items versus 5-7% on open-market items.

qa_highlights.question: Main board migration timing and FY28 Amzen contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Eligibility requires 1 crore shares (company at 92 lakh, expected to reach 1.02 crore after warrant and swap listings); BSE process 2-3 months, so migration likely in Q4 FY27. Amzen first production expected about three months after approval, with 25% capacity in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Spring RDSO approval and PAT margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said RDSO approval received but field trials (about 3,000 sets over six months) are pending; once done, orders and rates should improve, boosting PAT margins.

qa_highlights.question: When will the Amzen NCLT approval come and how many hearings remain?
qa_highlights.answer: Next hearing is 25 November; management said documents of 2,000-4,000 pages were filed and approval is procedural since the COC has approved; it did not rule out further delay into December.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue target for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 20-25% growth on FY26 revenue, citing stock to be pushed out in Q3 and new orders.

risks_watch: Amzen NCLT final approval timing (next hearing 25 November 2026) and the INR 60 crore payment; delays push back production.
Forging unit and springs field trials: commissioning slipped 2-2.5 months; field-trial outcome determines spring pricing and volumes.
H1 revenue decline and reliance on H2 seasonality to meet 20-25% FY27 growth target.
Government railway and infrastructure funding flow; management cites West Asia crisis and fiscal deficit slowing orders.
Amzen operational ramp: job-work model in Punjab, approval lead times (ISO, BIS, RDSO, DRDO) and working capital needs.
Main board migration depends on share count and BSE approval of swaps.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term growth and Amzen, but cautious and defensive on H1 softness and the Amzen approval delays; the CMD repeatedly explained the slowdown as seasonal and government-funding driven, and some answers were loosely specific on numbers.
key_quotes: So the best case scenario is we did INR 717 crores last year.
The first quarter is always the weakest. The second quarter becomes better. Third quarter becomes really good. The fourth quarter becomes top.
We are still looking at it and we are very hopeful we'll achieve it also because we are carrying a lot of stock, a lot of plans for pushing the stock out in the first third quarter itself.

growth.why: Management reiterated 20-25% FY27 revenue growth despite H1 standalone revenue falling from INR 161 crore to INR 151 crore; backing is a INR 612 crore order book (up ~39-40%) and capacity coming live (springs to 24-25k MT and forging by Apr-May 2027), but H2 relies on seasonally stronger Q3/Q4 with no contracted quantification of the step-up.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Springs at ~15% PAT margin (INR 30,000 sale vs INR 22,500 cost) and forging targeted at 14-15% PAT, versus 5-7% on open-market items, but both depend on field trials and April-May 2027 commercial runs; H1 standalone revenue fell to INR 151 crore from INR 161 crore.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Springs rise from 13,600 MT to 24,000-25,000 MT by end FY27 and forging (10,000-11,000 MT, INR 45-50 crore) targets Apr-May 2027, but set-up slipped 2-2.5 months and Amzen (~150,000 MT) hinges on NCLT approval with hearing on 25 Nov 2026 and possible slip into December.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Order book INR 612 crore is up ~39-40% YoY and a new wagon order of INR 900-1,000 crore (10,000 wagons) was won in October, but H1 standalone revenue fell 6% (INR 151 crore vs 161 crore) at 78.6% utilisation, so the H2 step-up is not yet proven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 78.6% (near the 80% threshold) and the company is already committing INR 45-50 crore to forging, INR 60 crore to Amzen and a galvanising air-wiping facility to be announced by end Nov 2026; further capex is plausible but not firmly guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated only 20-25% FY27 revenue growth on FY26 despite H1 standalone revenue falling 6%, so an upgrade would need H2 to materially outrun the H1 shortfall.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 20-25% growth needs a sharp H2 step-up from a H1 revenue decline, forging slipped 2-2.5 months, and Amzen approval could slip into December, pushing its contribution out.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Forging (commercial runs Apr-May 2027) and springs RDSO field trials (about 3,000 sets over six months) could open new product lines, but timing depends on trial outcomes and set-up delays.

rows.label: Amzen acquisition completion (NCLT approval)
rows.why: Next NCLT hearing 25 Nov 2026 with procedural approval since COC approved, but further delay into December is not ruled out; INR 32 crore paid plus INR 28 crore deposit; first production about three months after approval, targeting 25% of ~150,000 MT in FY28.

rows.label: Main board migration
rows.why: Company at 92 lakh shares needs 1 crore, expected to reach 1.02 crore after warrant and swap listings; BSE process 2-3 months.

rows.label: Wagon order conversion with 30% option clause
rows.why: New wagon order of INR 900-1,000 crore (10,000 wagons) received end October 2026 and two orders from listed wagon makers to be posted after Diwali, supporting the INR 612 crore order book.

tone.note: Management was confident on Amzen, springs/forging capacity and the new wagon order, but cautious and defensive on H1 standalone revenue decline and Amzen approval delays; analysts pushed on the H2 step-up needed for the 20-25% FY27 growth target.
